question: What organ acts as the lungs and kidneys for a developing fetus?
explanation: Before birth, the placenta handles oxygen exchange and waste removal since the fetal lungs and kidneys are not yet functional. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h1)

question: Why does very little blood flow through the fetal lungs before birth?

options.A: The liver absorbs all the blood first
options.B: The heart pumps too weakly to reach the chest
options.C: The lungs are filled with fluid and do not exchange gas
options.D: Umbilical arteries block the path to the chest

explanation: Since the placenta provides oxygen, the fluid-filled fetal lungs need only minimal blood for nourishment, bypassing the rest. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h1)

question: Which fetal structure allows blood to flow directly from the right atrium to the left atrium?
explanation: The foramen ovale is an opening between the upper heart chambers that lets blood skip the right ventricle and lungs. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h2)

question: What is the main job of the ductus arteriosus?

options.A: Connects the pulmonary artery to the aorta
options.B: Connects the umbilical vein to the liver
options.C: Carries waste back to the placenta
options.D: Seals the opening between the two atria

explanation: The ductus arteriosus diverts blood from the pulmonary artery straight into the aorta, bypassing the fluid-filled lungs. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h2)

question: What is the main trigger that causes blood vessels in the newborn lungs to relax and open?

options.B: The sudden release of adrenal hormones
options.C: The physical drop in environmental temperature
options.D: Exposure to oxygen from the first breath

explanation: Oxygen is a powerful natural vasodilator; when air enters the lungs, the sudden oxygen increase relaxes the pulmonary blood vessels. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h3)

question: What physical event causes a sudden rise in the newborn's systemic blood pressure?

options.B: The baby crying for the first time

explanation: Cutting the cord removes the low-resistance placenta, which sharply increases resistance and pressure in the systemic circulation. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h3)

question: How do pressures in the lungs and body change right after birth?

options.A: Both lung and body resistance drop together
options.B: Lung resistance drops while body resistance rises
options.C: Both lung and body resistance increase together
options.D: Lung resistance rises while body resistance drops

explanation: Expanding the lungs lowers pulmonary resistance, while cutting the placenta raises systemic resistance. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h4)

question: A newborn baby experiences cold stress, leading to low oxygen levels in the blood. What is most likely to happen to their lung blood vessels?

options.A: They will dilate and drop lung resistance further
options.B: They will convert directly into permanent ligaments
options.C: They will constrict and keep lung resistance high
options.D: They will force the ductus venosus to stay open

explanation: Low oxygen and cold stress cause pulmonary blood vessels to squeeze shut, maintaining high pulmonary resistance and stalling transition. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h4)

question: Why does the foramen ovale close immediately after birth?

options.A: The umbilical cord clamp pushes blood into the heart chambers
options.B: Cold air causes the flap tissue to freeze together
options.C: Muscles in the atrial wall contract and seal the hole shut
options.D: Pressure in the left atrium becomes higher than the right atrium

explanation: Blood returning from the newly opened lungs raises left atrial pressure, pushing the flap of the foramen ovale closed. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h5)

question: What is the difference between functional and anatomical closure of fetal shunts?

options.A: Functional closure requires surgery, while anatomical closure happens naturally
options.B: Functional closure stops blood flow immediately, while anatomical closure takes time to turn into tissue
options.C: Functional closure happens in the liver, while anatomical closure happens only inside the heart
options.D: Functional closure is permanent, while anatomical closure happens temporarily during crying

explanation: Shunts first stop working mechanically (functional), and later tissue grows to seal them permanently (anatomical). [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h5)

question: Where does blood go immediately after leaving the right side of the newborn's heart?
explanation: The right side of the heart pumps deoxygenated blood through the pulmonary arteries directly to the lungs for oxygen. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h6)

question: Which heart chamber is responsible for pumping freshly oxygenated blood out to the rest of the newborn's body?
explanation: The left ventricle receives oxygenated blood from the lungs and pumps it into the aorta to supply the systemic circulation. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h6)

question: A newborn is experiencing severe breathing trouble and low oxygen levels. What happens to the blood vessels in the baby's lungs as a result?

options.A: They stop pumping blood back to the right atrium
options.B: They stay constricted, keeping pulmonary resistance high
options.C: They dilate widely to let extra blood flow through
options.D: They turn into permanent fibrous ligaments right away

explanation: Low oxygen causes pulmonary blood vessels to squeeze shut, preventing the normal drop in resistance needed for healthy transition. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h7)

question: Which of the following conditions is characterized by high lung pressure and the failure of fetal shunts to close properly after birth?

options.A: Congenital liver failure from the ductus venosus
options.D: Persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn

explanation: PPHN occurs when high pulmonary resistance persists, keeping fetal shunts open and starving the body of oxygen. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h7)
